doc.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Lloyd Price, Motown, Woody Herman and Europe
title: Moving to Detroit as Motown's conductor
summary: Motown hired him to conduct and plan a jazz label, then balked; he conducted Stevie Wonder and others on tour.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: How does this fit with your Motown experience?
That was after all of this. Motown finally wanted to do – they wanted to have a jazz label. So they were going to let me . . .
So let me be clear. You weren’t a part of the Motown in Detroit.
Yeah, yes I was.
Okay.
I lived in Detroit at this time. I moved to Detroit for this.
Specifically to do this?
Conduct for them and all of that stuff.
Okay. All right. Let me back out then.

Yeah, I was there with Motown. It was a fantastic experience, because they were very successful. So they paid me well. They put me up in a hotel before a month. I didn’t have to do anything. They said, just have everything you want, all the steaks and lobster and everything. And they paid me besides that, and I wasn’t working. More than I was getting anywhere with any of the bands that I worked with. Then finally they were going to start a jazz . . .
Is this before you went to Europe with Woody Herman?
Yeah.
So we’re ’65, ’67.
Somewhere around there.
Somewhere in there.
They were going to start the label. So I was going to do that for them. It scared them to try to start a jazz label. That was frightening to them. So they finally didn’t do it.

Later, when they went to California, they started a MoJazz label. That’s why I started to interrupt you. But you’re actually talking about when they were still in Detroit, still in the old house, and all of that.
Detroit, yeah.
Did you do any writing for any of the pop things that were going on.
Not really. I conducted everything. I was a conductor. Then I was finally working with the Four Tops, after. I had conducted Stevie Wonder, some big shows that they had, and things like that.
So, conducting touring or studio stuff?
No, just touring. Never in the studio.
So Stevie – the Motown Review comes to the Apollo Theater, and they got a band, and you’re conducting it.
Yeah.
In the back of this is this idea that you’re doing this kind of stuff, but also decided they’re going to start a label, and at some point the label idea went away, and then you went away.
I felt I needed the experience as a conductor. I needed that experience. So for that reason it was good. Then this time . . .
